purpose: Reference set of recently recorded, real astronomical events across four phenomenon classes (gravitational waves, gamma-ray bursts, supernovae, high-energy neutrinos), for use as class-object reference data. Generated by direct web search against live archives on 2026-08-02, not reconstructed from training memory.
important_caveats: This is NOT a complete top-10 pull from each archive's raw database -- it is the set of events that could be independently verified with real sourced details in this session. Counts vary by category (7-9 events) rather than being padded to exactly 10.

Gravitational waves: the formal, peer-reviewed catalog (GWTC-5.0) only extends through 2025-01-28 (end of observing sub-run O4b). A third sub-run, O4c, ran June-November 2025 and would contain more recent events, but those are not yet in the peer-reviewed catalog and specific event names were not found in this search session -- flagged as a known gap.

Gamma-ray bursts and neutrino alerts are sourced from GCN (General Coordinates Network) circulars, which are preliminary community reports, not peer-reviewed papers. Positions and fluxes may be refined in later circulars.

Supernovae: many 2026 transients on TNS/ATLAS/ZTF are still unclassified ('AT2026xxx' designation). Only spectroscopically CONFIRMED supernovae (assigned 'SN' designation with a type) are included here.

Detector/instrument status at time of writing: LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA network is between observing runs (O4 completed Nov 18 2025; next run IR1 planned Oct/Nov 2026) -- no new GW detections are occurring as of this file's generation date.

gravitational_waves.source: LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Collaboration, GWTC-5.0 catalog (arXiv:2605.27223, 2605.27225) and associated LIGO Lab / Caltech press releases
gravitational_waves.notes: These are the most recent AND most scientifically significant events from the final segment of O4 (O4b, through Jan 28 2025), not a raw chronological dump -- selected because they had verifiable, specific reported parameters.

events.significance: Highest SNR gravitational wave signal observed to date; used to confirm Hawking's black hole area theorem
Primary black hole spinning opposite to orbital direction -- first observed instance
One of the fastest-rotating black holes observed to date; enabled precision test of general relativity / Kerr solution
High SNR enabled informative astrophysical measurement of GW detector calibration
Best-localized gravitational wave source observed to date -- 6 square degrees sky area, via 3-detector triangulation
Largest binary black hole merger yet detected as of 2025; final mass exceeds 200 solar masses, challenging stellar evolution models
Highest inspiral spin observed -- both components spinning at roughly 40% the speed of light

gamma_ray_bursts.source: GCN (General Coordinates Network), NASA -- Fermi GBM, SVOM, GECAM, MAXI detections
gamma_ray_bursts.notes: Ordered most recent first, based on GCN circulars found in this session. All dates in 2026.

events.significance: Associated with spectroscopically classified supernova SN 2026fgk (12th GRB-SN found within 1 Gpc since 1998); optical afterglow among the brightest ever observed, exceeding GRB 221009A

events.classification: long GRB, two-episode FRED light curve

supernovae.source: Transient Name Server (TNS, official IAU mechanism), ePESSTO+, Astronomer's Telegram
supernovae.notes: Restricted to spectroscopically CONFIRMED supernovae only (excludes unclassified 'AT' transients, which make up the bulk of recent TNS entries).

events.notes: Template matching consistent with both normal SN Ia and subluminous SN1986G-like subtype

events.significance: 12th GRB-supernova found within 1 Gpc since 1998; 15th Ic-BL supernova associated with a prompt high-energy transient

events.classification_basis: narrow hydrogen emission lines in optical spectra

supernovae.known_gap: TNS AstroNote 2026-120 and 2026-166 (ePESSTO+ classification reports, June-July 2026) confirmed multiple additional Type Ia and Type II supernovae in this window but individual SN designations/coordinates were not resolved in this search session -- would need direct TNS query for full extraction.

neutrino_detections.source: IceCube Neutrino Observatory, distributed via GCN (General Coordinates Network)
neutrino_detections.notes: IceCube 'Gold'/'Bronze' real-time alerts are automated, moderate-confidence astrophysical neutrino candidates (Bronze: ~30% astrophysical purity), not confirmed detections in the sense of a GW or GRB -- flagged as such rather than presented as certain.

events.notes: No known gamma-ray source in Fermi LAT 16-year Source List within 90% uncertainty region
No known gamma-ray source in Fermi 4FGL-DR4 or 3FHL catalogs within 90% uncertainty region

neutrino_detections.known_gap: IceCube typically issues ~10 Gold + ~16 Bronze alerts per year combined -- only 3 individual alerts were resolved with full details in this search session. A direct query of the GCN IceCube mission event archive (gcn.nasa.gov/missions/icecube) would be needed to fill out a true last-10 list; that endpoint was not directly fetchable in this session due to tool access restrictions.
